lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: Add a short target-role descriptor or summary.
items.because: The intended focus on applied ML and ML systems is not immediately clear to recruiters.

items.says: Organize the short skills section by type of skill.
items.because: It mixes tools, methods, and broad capabilities, making them harder to distinguish.

items.says: Clarify what diagnostic accuracy means, its comparison baseline, and the evaluation scale or dataset.
items.because: Readers need context to interpret and trust the 35% improvement.

items.says: Clarify how reviewer disagreement was measured and what the percentages represent.
items.because: The basis of the reduction from 14% to 6% is unclear.

items.says: Make the specialist agents’ and reviewer’s roles easier to understand at a glance.
Give the evaluation scope or sample size for the tool-call reduction and equal-accuracy claim.
items.because: Readers will want to know how equal accuracy was established.

items.says: Make the penalized-call description understandable to a general ML hiring reader.
Clarify the practical significance of catching two accuracy regressions.
items.because: The release-related contribution could be clearer without overstating it.

items.says: Remove or substantially differentiate the repeated assistant-only loss-masking bullet.
items.because: The second mention adds no distinct evidence.

items.says: Clarify the backlog reduction’s comparison period or baseline.
items.because: The eight weeks after launch do not establish the starting point.

items.says: Clarify how the triage system, sensor signals, and backlog outcome relate.
The sensor-triage and backlog achievement is also presented under the Research-Agent project.
items.because: It reads like the same achievement was performed in two places, raising attribution questions.

items.says: Specify the memory measure or workload behind the 4× reduction.
items.because: The comparison needs measurement context.

items.says: Clarify the latency test conditions if they are not stated elsewhere.
items.because: The basis for the measured improvement is unclear.

items.says: Fix the present-tense verb form in the CI pipeline bullet.
items.because: The résumé describes this as a completed role.

items.says: Clarify how the pipeline work shortened release cycles to three days and what the previous cycle was.
items.because: The relationship between the work and the figure is unclear.

items.says: Specify how the elimination of nightly backlogs was verified, if accurate.
items.because: Readers may ask for evidence behind that outcome.

items.says: Make sure “Owner” reflects your actual level of ownership.
Replace the AI-first engineering practices bullet with a concrete, verifiable contribution or remove it.
items.because: Its broad, promotional language gives no evidence of what was built, how adoption was demonstrated, or what improved.

items.says: Clarify what the 100× comparison refers to.
items.because: A reader could interpret it in more than one way.

items.says: Clarify the test conditions behind “50-way fan-out.”
Clarify your share of the evaluation-metrics work.
items.because: The project lists you as a contributor.

items.says: State what the evaluator’s scores were correlated against.
items.because: Without that, the Kendall correlation is hard to interpret.

items.says: The triage and backlog result duplicates the internship achievement, including its 68% reduction in rounded form.
items.because: Presenting the same result as a separate accomplishment looks padded and raises attribution questions.

items.says: Make clearer what “agent evaluation” means in practice.
items.because: A reader may want to know what that broad capability involves.
